questions.question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

I __am wrote a weekly__ column for the local newspaper.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**write a weekly**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In the given sentence, the error lies in the usage of the verb "wrote." **
 
• **The verb form 'am wrote' is incorrect as it uses the past tense form of 'write' with the present tense auxiliary verb 'am'.**
 
• “Am” is the present tense (in the first person singular) of the verb “to be”.
 
• Option 1 correctly changes the verb form to the present tense 'write'.
 
• The correct sentence will be:
 
 
• I write a weekly__ column for the local newspaper.
 
 

Hence, **the correct answer is option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Option 2: 'Write a week' is not grammatically correct as it changes the verb and noun forms.
 
• Option 4: 'writes a weekly' is also correct grammatically, but it changes the subject-verb agreement as 'writes' is for third-person singular subject.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

If it ________ been for him, nobody would even have known Monster was back!
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**hadn't**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The sentence is in the past perfect tense, which is used to talk about an action that was completed before another past action.**

 
 
• **The formula for the past perfect tense is had + [past participle]. ​**
 
 
 
• The phrase "hadn't been" is the past perfect form of "have not been."
 
• **The sentence means that if he had not been there, no one would have known that Monster was back.**
 
• The word "even" emphasizes the idea that no one would have known about Monster's return. 
 
• Thus, the correct sentence will be:
 
 
• If it hadn't__ been for him, nobody would even have known Monster was back!
 
 

Hence, **the correct answer is option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1 - wasn't: This is the past simple form of "be," which is used to describe a state or condition. However, it doesn't fit the context of the sentence because it doesn't convey the idea of a completed action before another past action.
 
• Option 3 - couldn't: This is the past simple form of "can't," which is used to express inability or impossibility. However, it doesn't fit the context of the sentence because it doesn't convey the idea of a completed action before another past action.
 
• Option 4 - hasn't: This is the present perfect form of "have not," which is used to talk about a past action that has a connection to the present. However, it doesn't fit the context of the sentence because it doesn't convey the idea of a completed action before another past action.

• "Have been given" and "have to given" are both incorrect because they use the present tense "have" instead of the past tense.
 
• Also, "Was given" is the past tense verb form for a singular subject, but the subject in this sentence is plural.
 
 
 
• "Were given" is the correct past tense verb form for a plural subject.
